Estimates

Revenue and distributional estimates for Hawaiʻi tax and budget policy, from Hawaiʻi Appleseed’s open-source models. Every figure links to the data and code that produced it.

Current policy

Laws already on the books: what they raise or cost, and who is affected.

Income tax

Act 24

Hawaiʻi’s 2026 income tax law: lower rates for most households, a 13 percent top bracket, and narrower credits.

$739 million
more revenue over tax years 2027 to 2031
Model run September 26, 2026

Tax credits

Expiring Relief

The 2023 expansions of the earned income and food/excise tax credits end after 2027. What families lose, and what renewal would cost.

$78 million
less for working families in tax year 2028
Model run September 25, 2026

Proposed policy

Options before the Legislature or in public debate, scored against current law.

Capital gains

Closing the Gap

What taxing capital gains at 9 percent, or at ordinary rates, would raise under Act 24.

Conveyance tax

Top of the Market

Sliding-scale conveyance tax rates on home sales above about $2 million, as in the last draft of SB 3028. What they would raise, county by county, and who would pay.

$78 million
per year, fiscal year 2028, after fewer sales
